title: COUNT and the NULLs
reveal:
3. COUNT(expr) counts the rows where expr IS NOT NULL, so the two NULL scores are skipped - and duplicates still count, so the two 10s are two.

Three counts on the same table, all different:

    COUNT(*)                5   -- rows, NULLs and all
    COUNT(score)            3   -- non-NULL values
    COUNT(DISTINCT score)   2   -- distinct non-NULL values: 10 and 30

Every aggregate skips NULLs the same way, which is why AVG(score) here is (10 + 30 + 10) / 3, not the same 50 divided by 5 rows. And over a group with no non-NULL values every aggregate returns NULL - except COUNT, which returns 0. That is the difference behind COALESCE(SUM(x), 0): SUM needs it, COUNT never does.
